name: Butyl acetate
description: Butyl acetate (CAS 123-86-4 ), also known as NBA, is a fast-evaporating ester solvent used across coatings, personal care, and flavor manufacturing. FEMA 2174 designates its use as a food-grade flavoring ingredient. In food applications, it delivers a characteristic fruity note. Its evaporation profile and solvency strength make it a preferred carrier in formulations requiring clean, residue-free drying for industrial use. In nail care and cosmetic formulations, butyl acetate is the primary solvent in nail lacquers and polish removers, controlling viscosity and film formation. It ensures a smooth application and quick drying time. Coatings and adhesives manufacturers use it to dissolve nitrocellulose, acrylics, and vinyl resins in industrial and automotive finishing systems. It is essential for high-performance surface coatings and resins. As a FEMA-approved flavoring agent, it is used in confectionery, beverages, and baked goods to impart apple and pear flavor profiles. It meets the strict requirements for food-grade chemical additives. In metalworking and lubricant blending, it functions as a carrier solvent for cutting fluids and surface treatment formulations. It is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities. Standard commercial grades include technical and industrial purity levels suited for coatings and metalworking applications. Food-grade and flavor-grade material is available to meet FCC specifications. These high-purity grades are necessary for use in regulated food and cosmetic applications.
